study.question: Can a field-specific correction of opposing auxiliary-to-context derivatives retain the complementary information lost by dropping whole auxiliary tasks or outcome groups, and outperform both ordinary joint gradients and a magnitude-only control?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: the current shared/live-context incumbent has click AUC 0.6662458901 versus 0.6659481623 when auxiliary context gradients are blocked. Cart/fav-only and buy-only derivatives produce 0.6662117095 and 0.6661861763. In the latest same-hook suite, both outcomes give 0.6662241275, positives only 0.6647485962, negatives only 0.6651540446 and neither 0.6659481623. Thus blanket removal loses useful complementary signal; these outcomes do not yet demonstrate gradient conflict. Provisional mechanism: fields can contain opposing auxiliary and primary derivatives even when their concatenated inner product is nonnegative. Removing only the opposing component of the aggregate auxiliary context derivative may preserve useful remaining signal. This deliberately tests, rather than assumes, the conflict explanation. The earlier positional projection obtained 0.6641686829, norm control 0.6640651250, and primary-only 0.6655179496, so projection is not presumed effective.

inherited_components: All incumbent g3-r0022-selector_disabled modules, task towers, embedding tables, private auxiliary item tables and detached private auxiliary selector inputs.

study.proposed_difference: Add a declared training_loss and ephemeral common-context cache to the supplied incumbent; introduce no parameters, learned gates or RNG draws. Compute two partial VJPs from the same training forward: click and summed auxiliary BCEs to the common [B,F*16] context. Reshape to [B,F,16], calculate field projection, projected-norm scaling and global projection in every cell, then select one correction. Return sum(mean four FP32 BCEs) plus <context-stop(context), stop(selected_aux-original_aux)>. The scalar surrogate is zero at finite states. Before host clipping, the context derivative is p+selected_aux while all task-tower and other-edge derivatives remain ordinary BCE. Unlike round25, no positives/negatives are dropped and no extra context tables/cloned forward branches are allocated. The projection metric treats input occurrences separately: shared IDs and adaptive optimizers prevent a parameter- or update-space guarantee. Originality is explicitly unverified; the authorized registry search did not supply a primary gradient-surgery paper, and no priority claim is made.
predictions: At fixed weights and input, all four variant predictions and full BCE scalar values agree. No labels enter forward; inference remains identical in computation structure. Expected capacity remains incumbent 56,407,643 total parameters (56,054,432 embedding, 353,211 dense), pending host confirmation.

Host gradient checks at the shared context edge should give p+selected_aux, with per-field <p_f,projected_aux_f> >= 0 up to FP32 tolerance and no projected field norm increase. Tower/selector/item gradients should equal the ordinary same-hook derivatives before host clipping. Zero primary fields retain auxiliary derivatives; zero auxiliary fields remain zero.

If field-specific opposition is consequential, field_project should improve click AUC by at least 0.0001 over the new joint control and exceed field_norm. Field/global ordering tests localization; it is not assumed. Report all four task AUC/Logloss and auxiliary mean separately without selecting on them.

No inference speedup is predicted. Training incurs two extra tower-to-context VJPs plus small FP32 reductions; model-only latency, throughput, peak memory, training/allocated GPU seconds, wall time and examples must be measured by the host.

Use existing history slices empty/1-16/17-64/>64, reporting samples and positives/negatives, as exploratory diagnostics. Any extra field-frequency, time or composition bins require training-only definitions and host-available inputs; no unsupplied timestamp/frequency data is invented.
falsifiers: Failed loss/forward equality, incorrect context derivative, changed other-edge derivatives before clipping, parameter .grad accumulation during VJP probes, nonfinite values or label-dependent predictions invalidates the implementation before a mechanism comparison.
Field_project failing to beat the joint same-hook endpoint rejects this implementation as an improvement. Winning only against historical endpoints does not pass the within-suite contrast.
Field_norm matching or beating field_project leaves magnitude suppression sufficient; no direction-specific claim. Global_project matching or winning leaves field granularity unsupported.

Observed opposition is absent or tiny: no support that gradient opposition is the relevant bottleneck. Opposition removed without a validation gain: local geometric property is not predictive mechanism evidence.

A one-seed gain reversed by authorized paired repetitions or paired user-cluster intervals is not robust support. Failed cost/memory preflight or exceeding the fixed 1203.368969-second trial cap makes the proposed implementation infeasible, not scientifically refuted.
A subsequent authorized primary-source audit establishes an equivalent method: revise the prior-work difference. General gradient surgery, context routing and surrogate gradients are not claimed new.
alternative_explanations: Projection is in context-occurrence coordinates, not shared embedding parameter or Adagrad update coordinates. Repeated IDs/tied encoders can invalidate parameter-space alignment; no descent guarantee is claimed.

The norm control matches each projected field norm at the same instantaneous state; different training trajectories need not remain norm matched.
This is exploratory after many validation-selected trials. One seed, no paired user-cluster uncertainty and no held-out outcomes cannot establish a general mechanism.
Auxiliary shared context may already be beneficial with little consequential conflict; dropping outcomes may primarily distort balance/calibration rather than expose interference.
An apparent gain can arise from changed optimization magnitude, sparse-ID frequency weighting, fixed BCE clamp, BF16 cancellation, batch composition, selection noise or different task calibration.
Previous field/task/position improvements include capacity and optimization changes; the total baseline-to-incumbent difference cannot be assigned to the current proposed context mechanism.
